record.paper_title: Conformally invariant scaling limits: an overview and a collection of problems
record.original_question: Let f_ℓ be the Boolean crossing function for critical site percolation in an approximately ℓ×ℓ square of the triangular lattice, and let ˜μ_{f_ℓ} denote the induced probability measure on Fourier-Walsh levels |S|. Is it true that ˜μ_{f_ℓ}([ℓ^{α_1}, ℓ^{α_2}]) tends to 1 as ℓ tends to infinity whenever α_1 < 3/4 < α_2? More generally, determine the asymptotic behavior of ˜μ_{f_ℓ}([ℓ^{α_1}, ℓ^{α_2}]) for arbitrary 0 ≤ α_1 < α_2 ≤ 2.

evidence.quote: Problem 5.1. Is it true that limℓ→∞ ˜µfℓ([ℓα1, ℓα2]) = 1 if α1 < 3/4 < α2? Determine the asymptotic behavior of ˜µfℓ([ℓα1, ℓα2]) as ℓ → ∞ for arbitrary 0 ≤ α1 < α2 ≤ 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider critical site percolation on the triangular lattice, in which each site is independently coloured black or white with probability 1/2. For a positive integer ℓ, let D_ℓ denote an approximately ℓ×ℓ square region of the triangular lattice with two designated opposite sides, and let f_ℓ : {-1,+1}^{D_ℓ} → {-1,+1} be the Boolean crossing function whose value is +1 if and only if there is a black path in D_ℓ connecting the two designated sides. Expand f_ℓ in the Fourier–Walsh basis,
   f_ℓ = Σ_{S ⊂ D_ℓ} f̂_ℓ(S) χ_S,
where χ_S(ω) = Π_{x∈S} ω(x). Define the spectral probability measure on subsets S ⊂ D_ℓ by P̂_ℓ(S) = f̂_ℓ(S)^2 (which sums to 1 because f_ℓ takes values ±1), and let μ̃_{f_ℓ} be the law of the (random) cardinality |S| under P̂_ℓ; thus μ̃_{f_ℓ} is a probability measure on {0,1,…,|D_ℓ|}.

(a) Prove or disprove: for every 0 ≤ α_1 < 3/4 < α_2,
        μ̃_{f_ℓ}([ℓ^{α_1}, ℓ^{α_2}]) → 1   as ℓ → ∞.

(b) More generally, determine the asymptotic behaviour of μ̃_{f_ℓ}([ℓ^{α_1}, ℓ^{α_2}]) as ℓ → ∞ for arbitrary 0 ≤ α_1 < α_2 ≤ 2.
artifact.status_search_result: The concentration question in part (a) was resolved affirmatively by Garban, Pete and Schramm in "The Fourier spectrum of critical percolation" (Acta Mathematica 205 (2010), 19–104), who proved that the spectral mass of f_ℓ concentrates on cardinalities of order ℓ^{3/4} (the conjectured pivotal/spectral exponent), giving sharp lower-tail estimates. A complete description of the asymptotic behaviour of μ̃_{f_ℓ}([ℓ^{α_1}, ℓ^{α_2}]) for all 0 ≤ α_1 < α_2 ≤ 2 (in particular near the endpoints and at finer scales than power-law concentration) does not appear to be fully established; the existence of a scaling limit of the spectral sample as a random Cantor-like set of Hausdorff dimension 3/4 has subsequently been obtained, but precise fluctuation asymptotics for the windowed mass remain partial.

status_evidence.title: The Fourier spectrum of critical percolation
status_evidence.snippet: Sharp bounds for the lower tail of the Fourier spectrum of the percolation crossing function, proving concentration around the pivotal/spectral exponent 3/4.
status_evidence.claim: Concentration of spectral mass around scale ℓ^{3/4} (part (a)) is established.

status_evidence.title: The Fourier spectrum of critical percolation, Acta Mathematica
status_evidence.snippet: Garban, Pete, Schramm obtain sharp bounds on the lower tail of the spectral measure for the crossing event, with applications to dynamical and near-critical percolation.
status_evidence.claim: The 3/4 concentration conjecture for the spectral measure is proved.
